precedenceRule: The live funding opportunity and current agency application guide always override this repository.

nih_rpg_srf.label: NIH Research Project Grant — Simplified Review Framework
draftOrder: Human Subjects and Other Required Plans

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.pageRule: Usually 1 page unless the NOFO says otherwise.

sections.name: Innovation
requiredSignals: conceptual, technical, methodological, implementation, or use-of-existing-methods innovation
why the innovation changes expected impact

sections.name: Expertise and Resources
requiredSignals: explicit gap closure when expertise or resources are missing

reviewFramework.reviewQuestion: Should the proposed research be conducted?
Can the proposed research be conducted well?
Are the expertise and resources in place to do it?

writingRules: Draft Specific Aims early and use it as the controlling architecture for the rest of the application.
Do not write aims as a list of experiments; each aim should state a bounded objective and expected contribution.
Make the scientific gap and expected impact explicit before introducing detailed methods.
Tie risks and alternative strategies to each aim rather than placing generic contingency language at the end.
Keep budget, personnel effort, milestones, and approach internally consistent.
Write titles, abstracts, and public-health relevance statements in plain language for a broad educated audience.
Treat the live NOFO, FORMS-I instructions, and NIH Guide notices as authoritative.

nih_small_business.label: NIH SBIR/STTR
draftOrder: Human Subjects and Other Required Plans

reviewFramework.reviewQuestion: Is the R&D important, feasible, and appropriate for the small-business mechanism?
Can the proposed R&D plausibly translate into a usable, sustainable product or service?

writingRules: Separate research and development risk from routine product implementation.
Make Phase I or early-phase milestones objective and measurable.
Do not treat commercialization as a generic market-size paragraph; connect technical success to a defined customer, purchaser, or implementation route.
For STTR, reconcile workshare and research-institution responsibilities before narrative drafting.
Verify current small-business eligibility, registrations, budget limits, and solicitation-specific instructions before submission.

nsf_research.label: NSF Research Proposal

sections.name: Project Summary
sections.pageRule: 1 page under current general NSF guidance.

sections.name: Project Description
sections.pageRule: Typically 15 pages under current general NSF guidance; solicitation-specific rules prevail.

reviewFramework.reviewQuestion: What is the potential to advance knowledge?
What is the potential to benefit society and contribute to desired societal outcomes?

writingRules: State what will be done, why it matters, how it will be done, how success will be known, and what benefits may follow.
Treat Broader Impacts as an executable workstream with beneficiaries, activities, ownership, milestones, and evaluation rather than generic benefit language.
Keep Results from Prior NSF Support distinct and current when required.
Prepare senior/key personnel documents and other Research.gov components outside the narrative compiler when required by NSF systems.
Verify the current PAPPG, supplements, and solicitation because NSF policy is undergoing revision.

samhsa_discretionary.label: SAMHSA Discretionary Grant

reviewFramework.reviewQuestion: Does each scored criterion have an explicit, easy-to-find response?

writingRules: Use the exact NOFO section headings and scoring order whenever possible.
Build a requirement-to-section crosswalk before drafting prose.
Map every budget line to a proposed activity, staffing requirement, or deliverable.
Use performance measures and implementation milestones that can be reported during the award.
Do not assume forms or attachments from an older SAMHSA cycle remain current.

generic_research.label: Generic Research / Foundation Proposal
draftOrder: Executive Summary or Letter of Intent

reviewFramework.reviewQuestion: Does the proposal answer the funder's stated priorities and review criteria directly?

writingRules: Create a scored-criteria crosswalk before drafting.
Separate evidence of need from claims about intervention effectiveness.
Use measurable objectives and tie each to activities, responsible roles, timing, evaluation, and budget.
Treat the funder's live instructions as authoritative.
